notes:
Diagnosis 2026-11-21 from the 10 seed captures of tools/classify_rules_eval.py (job 6b0130d0efaf5e14f4b46b34), no new simulation. (1) The ship gives 11-13 confirmed tracks on every seed, all within 170 m of it, at ranges from the true range (11,853 m) to about 130 m beyond: its arrivals by longer paths in 100 m of water. Nearly every one has about the ship's velocity (5-7 m/s west). (2) The gallery scores the ship by the NEAREST track to the truth; with a dozen copies that is a coin toss among them (often a short 4-point track born at ping 3, which cannot be a mover from 4 points, or a multipath child): the 3-of-10 and the '3.3 m/s' (k0 id 9, 4 points, rms 21 m) come from this. Reproduced: nearest track mover on k4, k5, k7 exactly. (3) Echo grouping takes the STRONGEST track as the object and only groups weaker tracks FARTHER out in range. The strongest arrival is 50-83 m beyond the true range on every seed (a later path, not the direct one); the earliest arrival (within 3 m of the true range on 9 of 10 seeds) is weaker, so it and other early arrivals are never grouped: 3-6 tracks stay mover/uncertain per seed. (4) Only 6 pings (20 s apart), so tracks born after ping 2 have 4 points and stay uncertain by the Student-t rule. Not a tracker velocity bug. Fix options for the owner: scoring by object (any non-multipath track within the gate, or the group), grouping that takes the earliest arrival as the object or groups both sides in range, more pings in the scenario.

Fixed by D-155 (merged): echo grouping transitive on both sides, object = earliest established arrival; gallery scores the object. Re-score of 120 captures: ship one mover on 10/10 seeds. Gallery regeneration on GPU pending at the time of this note.
